name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The moderator aims to easily create, configure, and manage Planning Poker game sessions, including adding, editing, and deleting items for estimation, and inviting participants.
The moderator seeks to efficiently guide the team through the estimation process, including selecting items, revealing estimates, accepting agreed-upon values, and re-estimating when necessary.
The moderator wants to manage and access game data, including importing stories, browsing past games, viewing transcripts, and exporting results for further analysis.
The moderator expects to have a secure and flexible account to manage their profile, including creation, login, detail modification, and password recovery.
The moderator aims to configure game settings such as estimation scales and participant limits to best suit their team's preferences and size.
The estimator aims to easily join games, view items for estimation, submit their estimates, and understand the context of the current and past estimations.

The estimator seeks to contribute to discussions by seeing other participants' estimates, understanding changes in opinions, and utilizing tools like a countdown timer to facilitate focused conversations.
The participant desires clear visibility into who has estimated, the current item being estimated, and the history of estimates to ensure informed decision-making.
The participant expects a consistent display of information, such as card order and personal identifiers, to enhance usability and personal connection during the game.
The developer aims to build an application that adheres to web standards, performs efficiently, and is accessible to a broad user base across various browsers.
The user expects the application to respond quickly to their actions, offer clear and logical navigation through predictable URLs, and handle errors gracefully.
The user desires the ability to use various languages and characters within the application, ensuring flexibility and global usability.
The researcher aims to access game results in a non-identifiable format to conduct studies on estimation patterns and team dynamics without compromising privacy.
lowLevelGoals: The moderator can initiate a new game session, providing a name or identifier for the game.
The moderator can input and add a new story or task to the current game session for participants to estimate.
The moderator can modify the details of a story or task that has been added to the game session.
The moderator can remove a story or task from the current game session.
The moderator can generate and share a unique link or code to invite others to join their game.
The moderator can choose which story or task from the list will be estimated by the participants next.
The moderator can trigger the display of all participants' submitted estimates for the currently selected item.
The moderator can finalize and record a chosen estimate for the current story or task after discussion.
The moderator can reset the estimation process for the current story or task, allowing participants to submit new estimates.
The moderator can upload a file (e.g., CSV, JSON) containing stories to populate the game's estimation backlog.
The moderator can view a historical record of all games they have moderated.
The moderator can access a detailed log of events, estimates, and discussions from a completed game.
The moderator can download the final estimates and other relevant game data in a structured format (e.g., CSV, PDF).
The moderator can register for a new account by providing necessary credentials (e.g., email, password).
The moderator can authenticate themselves to access their personalized features and game data.
The moderator can update their profile information, such as username or email address.
The moderator can initiate a process to reset their password if they have forgotten it.
The moderator can choose from predefined estimation scales (e.g., Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes) for their game.
The moderator can define a limit on how many individuals can join a specific game session.
The estimator can enter a game session using an invitation link or code provided by the moderator.
The estimator can see the details of the story or task that is currently being estimated.
The estimator can select a value from the available estimation scale and submit it for the current story or task.
The estimator can access a record of items that have already been estimated and their accepted values.
The estimator can see the estimates submitted by other team members once the moderator reveals them.
The estimator can see when other participants update their estimates during a re-estimation round.
The estimator can view a visual timer indicating the remaining time for discussion on an item.
The participant can view indicators (e.g., checkmarks, colored names) next to each participant's name to know who has estimated.
The participant can clearly identify which story or task is currently being discussed and estimated.
The participant can review the accepted estimates for stories or tasks that have already been processed.
The participant expects the available estimation values (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 5) to always appear in the same sequence on their screen.
The participant expects their chosen name or a unique identifier to be displayed uniformly throughout the application.
The developer will implement code and design practices that comply with W3C guidelines for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
The developer will implement techniques such as code splitting, lazy loading, and asset compression to minimize page load times.
The developer will test and implement features to function correctly across major web browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
The developer will integrate features that make the application usable for individuals with disabilities, following WCAG guidelines.
The user expects the application to provide immediate feedback or state changes upon clicking buttons, submitting forms, or navigating.
The user expects consistent and logical URL structures that reflect the current page or state of the application.
The user expects the application to display understandable messages when an error occurs, guiding them on how to resolve the issue.
The user can type and view content in different languages, including those with non-Latin characters.
The user can enter and see a wide range of special characters and symbols without issues in text input areas.
The researcher can retrieve game data where all personally identifiable information of participants has been removed or obscured.
The researcher can apply filters to the anonymized game data to focus on specific subsets for analysis.
